what: A single vertical card (a three.js plane) passes through the page’s placeholder cells in turn on scroll — from when the top of the first cell reaches screen center until the center of the last cell reaches screen center, with scrub .75. Between cells it is joined by Catmull-Rom, tilts forward along the way (sin(π·u) × −.4 rad), and makes a half turn on the Y axis at every cell (the back face is mirrored left-right and .82 darker). The panel center bulges by the scroll speed followed at .12 per step × 40 (up to .45 of the max width), and is shaded by light from the upper left (ambient .65 · diffuse .45). As progress advances, the image is split into as many faces as there are and swapped

options.tilt: Forward tilt angle during travel (rad), default .4
options.bend: Max swell share (relative to panel width), default .45
options.z: z-index of the picture board (screen-fixed canvas), default 0 — laid behind the text
options.[data-fx-part=slot]: Positions the card passes through (two or more empty cells sized at the same ratio as the card)
options.[data-fx-part=face]: Card image — the image if img, otherwise draws the data-label text on a gray panel (swaps with progress if there are several)

note: three must be global (window.THREE) for this to run — if it is missing or reduced motion is set, nothing is drawn. If the placeholder is hidden on screen (width 0), that cell is skipped. Give the text side position and z-index so the card shows behind the text while it passes.
